column1: The fertile land of the Nile delta is being eroded along Egypt’s Mediterranean coast at an astounding rate, in some parts estimated at 100 metres per year.
column2: 尼罗河三角洲的肥沃土地正沿着埃及的地中海海岸以惊人的速度被侵蚀，在某些地区，侵蚀速度甚至达到了每年100米。

column1: In the past, land scoured away from the coastline by the currents of the Mediterranean Sea used to be replaced by sediment brought down to the delta by the River Nile, but this is no longer happening.
column2: 过去，地中海海流会冲走海岸边的泥土，尼罗河顺流带到三角洲的泥沙又会将其补上；如今，这种补充不再发生了。

column1: Up to now, people have blamed this loss of delta land on the two large dams at Aswan in the south of Egypt, which hold back virtually all of the sediment that used to flow down the river.
column2: 到目前为止，人们一直将这种三角洲土地的丧失归咎于埃及南部的阿斯旺两座大型水坝。这两座水坝几乎阻断了原本可以顺流而下的一切沉积物。

column1: Before the dams were built, the Nile flowed freely, carrying huge quantities of sediment north from Africa’s interior to be deposited on the Nile delta.
column2: 在修建水坝之前，尼罗河自由流淌，将非洲内陆大量泥沙向北输送，并在尼罗河三角洲沉积下来。

column1: This continued for 7,000 years, eventually covering a region of over 22,000 square kilometres with layers of fertile silt.
column2: 这种情况持续了7000年，最终覆盖了超过22,000平方公里的区域，层层堆积了肥沃的淤泥。

column1: Annual flooding brought in new, nutrient-rich soil to the delta region, replacing what had been washed away by the sea, and dispensing with the need for fertilizers in Egypt’s richest food-growing area.
column2: 每年的洪水都会给三角洲带来富含养分的新土，补回被海水冲走的泥土，也使这片埃及最富饶的粮食产区无需施肥。
column9: dispensing with the need for|使……不再需要

column1: But when the Aswan dams were constructed in the 20th century to provide electricity and irrigation, and to protect the huge population centre of Cairo and its surrounding areas from annual flooding and drought, most of the sediment with its natural fertilizer accumulated up above the dam in the southern, upstream half of Lake Nasser, instead of passing down to the delta.
column2: 可是，20世纪修建阿斯旺水坝，既是为了供电和灌溉，也是为了保护开罗这一人口密集区及其周边免遭每年的洪水和干旱。筑坝后，大部分含有天然肥分的泥沙都积存在大坝上游的纳赛尔湖南半部，没有继续流向三角洲。

column1: Now, however, there turns out to be more to the story.
column2: 不过，现在看来事情并不那么简单。

column1: It appears that the sediment-free water emerging from the Aswan dams picks up silt and sand as it erodes the river bed and banks on the 800-kilometre trip to Cairo.
column2: 看来，从阿斯旺大坝流出的无沉积物河水在通往开罗的800公里旅程中，会因侵蚀河床和河岸而沿途携带淤泥和沙子。

column1: Daniel Jean Stanley of the Smithsonian Institute noticed that water samples taken in Cairo, just before the river enters the delta, indicated that the river sometimes carries more than 850 grams of sediment per cubic metre of water - almost half of what it carried before the dams were built.
column2: 史密森学会的丹尼尔·让·斯坦利注意到，在开罗、也就是河水即将流入三角洲的地方取得的水样表明，有时每立方米河水携带的泥沙超过850克，接近建坝前含沙量的一半。

column1: ‘I’m ashamed to say that the significance of this didn’t strike me until after I had read 50 or 60 studies,’ says Stanley in Marine Geology.
column2: ‘说实话，直到阅读了50到60篇相关研究之后，我才意识到这件事的重要性，’斯坦利在《海洋地质学》杂志上如此说道。

column1: ‘There is still a lot of sediment coming into the delta, but virtually no sediment comes out into the Mediterranean to replenish the coastline.
column2: 目前，仍有大量的沉积物流入三角洲地区，但实际上几乎没有沉积物能够进入地中海，从而补充海岸线的补给。

column1: So this sediment must be trapped on the delta itself.’
column2: 因此，这些沉积物必定被困在三角洲本身上。

column1: Once north of Cairo, most of the Nile water is diverted into more than 10,000 kilometres of irrigation canals and only a small proportion reaches the sea directly through the rivers in the delta.
column2: 一旦离开开罗市，尼罗河的大部分水流会被引向超过10,000公里的灌溉渠道，只有一小部分水流能够直接通过三角洲的河流流入海洋。

column1: The water in the irrigation canals is still or very slow-moving and thus cannot carry sediment, Stanley explains.
column2: 斯坦利解释说，灌溉渠道中的水流动非常缓慢，因此无法携带沉积物。

column1: The sediment sinks to the bottom of the canals and then is added to fields by farmers or pumped with the water into the four large freshwater lagoons that are located near the outer edges of the delta.
column2: 泥沙沉到运河底部，随后，有的由农民施到田里，有的随水被抽入三角洲外围附近的四个大型淡水潟湖。

column1: So very little of it actually reaches the coastline to replace what is being washed away by the Mediterranean currents.
column2: 实际上，只有极少一部分沉积物能够到达海岸线，从而补充被地中海洋流冲走的物质。

column1: The farms on the delta plains and fishing and aquaculture in the lagoons account for much of Egypt’s food supply.
column2: 三角洲平原上的农场，加上潟湖里的捕捞和水产养殖，供应了埃及相当大一部分食物。

column1: But by the time the sediment has come to rest in the fields and lagoons it is laden with municipal, industrial and agricultural waste from the Cairo region, which is home to more than 40 million people.
column2: 然而，泥沙最终沉积在农田和潟湖时，已经夹带着来自开罗地区的大量城市、工业和农业废弃物，该地区居住着四千多万人。

column1: ‘Pollutants are building up faster and faster,’ says Stanley.
column2: 斯坦利说：“污染物正以越来越快的速度积聚。”

column1: Based on his investigations of sediment from the delta lagoons, Frederic Siegel of George Washington University concurs.
column2: 乔治·华盛顿大学的弗雷德里克·西格尔根据自己对三角洲潟湖沉积物的研究，也认同这一看法。

column1: ‘In Manzalah Lagoon, for example, the increase in mercury, lead, copper and zinc coincided with the building of the High Dam at Aswan, the availability of cheap electricity, and the development of major power-based industries,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“例如，曼扎拉潟湖里的汞、铅、铜和锌都增加了，这恰好与阿斯旺高坝的修建、廉价电力的供应以及大型耗电工业的发展发生在同一时期。”
column13: power-based industries|n. 依赖电力的工业

column1: Since that time the concentration of mercury has increased significantly.
column2: 从那时起，汞的浓度大幅上升。

column1: Lead from engines that use leaded fuels and from other industrial sources has also increased dramatically.
column2: 使用含铅燃料的发动机以及其他工业污染源所排放的铅含量也显著增加了。

column1: These poisons can easily enter the food chain, affecting the productivity of fishing and farming.
column2: 这些毒素很容易进入食物链，从而影响渔业和农业的产量。

column1: Another problem is that agricultural wastes include fertilizers which stimulate increases in plant growth in the lagoons and upset the ecology of the area, with serious effects on the fishing industry.
column2: 另一个问题是，农业废弃物中含有肥料，会促进潟湖内植物的生长，扰乱当地生态，给渔业带来严重影响。

column1: According to Siegel, international environmental organisations are beginning to pay closer attention to the region, partly because of the problems of erosion and pollution of the Nile delta, but principally because they fear the impact this situation could have on the whole Mediterranean coastal ecosystem.
column2: 西格尔说，国际环保组织正开始更加关注这一地区。原因之一是尼罗河三角洲的侵蚀和污染，更主要的原因是，他们担心这种局面可能影响整个地中海沿岸生态系统。
column4: pay closer attention to|更加关注
column11: coastal ecosystem|n. 沿岸生态系统

column1: But there are no easy solutions.
column2: 但并没有简单的解决办法。

column1: In the immediate future, Stanley believes that one solution would be to make artificial floods to flush out the delta waterways, in the same way that natural floods did before the construction of the dams.
column2: 斯坦利认为，短期内一种可行的方案是制造人工洪水，以冲刷三角洲的水路，就像大坝修建之前自然洪水曾经做的那样。

column1: He says, however, that in the long term an alternative process such as desalination may have to be used to increase the amount of water available.
column2: 不过，他认为从长远来看，可能需要采用诸如海水淡化这样的替代方法来增加可用的水资源量。
column3: in the long term|adv. 从长远来看

column1: ‘In my view, Egypt must devise a way to have more water running through the river and the delta,’ says Stanley.
column2: ‘在我看来，埃及应该想办法让更多的水流入这条河流以及三角洲地区，’斯坦利说道。

column1: Easier said than done in a desert region with a rapidly growing population.
column2: 在人口迅速增长的沙漠地区，说起来容易，做起来难。
